item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 221137
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM EDT Tue Sep 22 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Fay, located several hundred miles southwest of the Azores.

Far Eastern Tropical Atlantic:
A tropical wave is forecast to move off the coast of western Africa
tomorrow. Although environmental conditions are not expected to
be particularly conducive, some slow development of this system is
possible while it moves generally northwestward across the far
eastern Atlantic. Interests in the Cabo Verde Islands should
monitor the progress of this system as gusty winds and areas
of heavy rain are possible there by the end of the week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Tropical Depression Fay Public Advisory Number 13
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM GMT Tue Sep 22 2026 
000
WTNT31 KNHC 221446
TCPAT1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Fay Advisory Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 PM GMT Tue Sep 22 2026
 
...FAY WEAKENS TO A TROPICAL DEPRESSION...
...FORECAST TO BECOME A POST-TROPICAL CYCLONE LATER TODAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM GMT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...31.1N 34.6W
ABOUT 645 MI...1035 KM SW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...SW OR 230 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1010 MB...29.83 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM GMT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Fay was
located near latitude 31.1 North, longitude 34.6 West. The
depression is moving toward the southwest near 10 mph (17 km/h). A 
gradual turn toward the west-southwest and then west is expected 
through midweek.
 
Recent satellite wind data indicate that maximum sustained winds 
are now near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts. Fay is likely to 
degenerate into a post-tropical remnant low today.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1010 mb (29.83 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Tropical Depression Fay Forecast Discussion Number 13
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM GMT Tue Sep 22 2026 
662 
WTNT41 KNHC 221447
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Depression Fay Discussion Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 PM GMT Tue Sep 22 2026

Fay is currently comprised of a swirl of low- to mid-level clouds 
with no convection. A recent ASCAT-B overpass indicates that the 
maximum winds are now near 30 kt, and based on this the cyclone is 
downgraded to a tropical depression. Unless convection comes back 
in the next several hours, Fay should degenerate into a remnant low 
later today.

The system is moving southwestward, or 230/9 kt, as it rounds the
eastern periphery of a low- to mid-level ridge to its west. A turn 
toward the west-southwest and then the west is expected over the 
next day or two as the ridge strengthens and builds eastward to the 
north of Fay. Due to a slight southward shift in the guidance 
envelope, the new track forecast is a little south of the previous 
forecast.

Currently, Fay is in an environment of moderate northwesterly shear 
and dry air entrainment. While the dynamical models forecast the 
shear to subside during the next 24 h, they also forecast strong 
upper-level convergence over the system and continued dry air 
entrainment. Based on this and the model simulated satellite 
imagery, it appears unlikely that Fay will re-develop persistent 
organized convection after the shear decreases. Thus, the new 
intensity forecast follows the old forecast in showing a gradual 
weakening of the remnant low until dissipation near 120 h.
